name: Go Signal
timeframe: hourly (clock-aligned 60-minute bars) on a daily context

card.context: A leader in an uptrend that has already moved: above the 200-day and 50-day with a rising 20-day EMA, RS 80 or more, pulled back to support after a tight hourly flag. Green market, ideally the index itself being bought at its 20-day line.
card.pattern: Early in the session the stock trades under the prior day's close, often undercutting the flag low, the prior day's low or the 20-day EMA, and buyers push it back above the prior close in the first or second hourly candle.
card.trigger: RED TO GREEN on the hourly chart: a market order at the close of the hourly candle that goes back above the prior day's close, by the end of the second candle (11:00). The cross itself is the aggressive version.
card.stop: A few cents under the session's low at the time of entry; usually 1% to 2%. If it is more than about 3% away, size down or skip; never raise it to the reclaimed level.
card.failure_mode: A turn that comes after the second hourly candle is a pivot, not a Go Signal. The reclaim that does not follow through gives it back within hours; a day that closes back under the prior close is the warning.

a_plus: go.leadership: a true leader (RS 90+ on his rating) in a hot group, after a catalyst or a big move (go.already_moved); the market Green (go.market_reading); in Orange only if everything else grades A+ (F65)
go.at_support: a quiet, tight pullback into the rising 20-day EMA (or the 9 EMA in a fast leader); go.hourly_flag: a tight hourly flag with a higher low

go.open_shape: a gap down or a quick flush under the prior day's low or the flag low into the 20-day line, and a strong green hourly candle back above the prior close in the first candle (go.reclaim_window), on rising volume (go.volume)
go.stop_width: a stop of 2% or less under the day's low; the day closes in the top of its range; it moves within days (his minimum 3-7 day burst)
b_minus: go.ema20_rising: the 20-day EMA flat; go.at_support: price near the 50-day or the 200-day; go.already_moved: no prior move
go.reclaim_window: the turn only in the second candle, and weak
go.stop_width: a stop near or over 3%
go.market_reading: a Yellow market (smaller and fewer)
go.liquidity: a thin or cheap stock; the day closes weak (go.close_under_pc_warning)
no_trade: go.inv_no_reclaim: a turn after the second hourly candle (a pivot)
go.above_200 and go.above_50: a stock in a downtrend, under the 50-day or the 200-day
go.first_hour_under_pc: a gap up that never trades under the prior close
go.no_chase: more than 4% over the prior close; go.not_stretched: more than 10% over the 10-day
go.liquidity: under $10 or under $20 million a day (GIC, VGZ)

lookalikes.tell: Read the clock. A Go Signal must be back above the prior day's close by the end of the second hourly candle (11:00); a turn later in the day, however clean, is a 30-minute pivot bought over the pivot candle's high.

Ask what the cross is riding on. A bare red to green is a trigger that happens in about a third of all liquid sessions; the Go Signal needs the setup around it: a leader that already moved, a tight hourly flag, and a dip into the 20-day line or a marked level before the turn.

Name the line that was reclaimed. An Oops gaps below the prior day's LOW and closes back above it on the daily bar; the Go Signal's line is the prior day's CLOSE and the reclaim is read on the first two hourly candles, whatever the open did.

Count the sessions. A U&R undercuts a prominent prior swing low and must close back above it within 3 sessions on the daily chart; the Go Signal's undercut and reclaim happen inside the first two hours of one session and are measured against the prior close.

invalidations: Before the entry: no hourly close back above the prior close by the end of the second hourly candle; a later turn is a pivot (go.inv_no_reclaim).
Before the entry: the first hourly candle never trades under the prior close, a gap up (go.first_hour_under_pc).

Before the entry: the stock is under the 50-day or 200-day (go.above_50, go.above_200), the fill is more than 4% over the prior close (go.no_chase) or 10% over the 10-day (go.not_stretched), a report is within 3 sessions (go.earnings_window).
After the entry: a trade below the session low, the stop (go.after_entry_stop); a gap through it follows B20 (go.stop_gap).
After the entry: a close back under the prior close is a warning, not an exit (go.close_under_pc_warning); a close under the 50-day ends the pullback thesis (go.context_break).
mistakes: Buying the open before the turn: the blind open buy that gets stopped at the low.
Calling a 14:00 turn a Go Signal: it is a pivot.
Taking it in a downtrend, under the 50-day or 200-day.
Taking it on a cheap or thin stock (GIC, VGZ).
A stop wider than about 3% with full size.
Grading from the daily chart: the daily footprint cannot show the turn.
Mixing it up with the Model Book card's pattern (a catalyst gap, a dip to the 9 EMA, an engulfing day), which is a different setup.
Ignoring the bar setting: the same session can pass on one chart and fail on another.
Treating the turn itself as the edge: it happens in about a third of all liquid sessions; the stock and the level are the edge.
Chasing past 4% or buying right before earnings.

short_mirror.note: A downside go signal (green to red), D47 mirrored: below the 200-day SMA only (B26), RS 20 or less (C31 mirror), a stock that has fallen and bounced into resistance (a falling 20-day EMA, the 50-day, a bearish gap); the first hourly candle trades above the prior close and an hourly candle closes back under it by the second candle; short at market; stop a few cents over the session high. The journal already has a Green to Red tag. He was not interested ('Maybe a downside go signal but who cares'); the dossier recommends teaching it only as the mirror in one lesson or leaving it out, as he decides (D-001; question 13). Leveraged inverse ETFs (E54) are another way UCT expresses it (Bracco's SOXS). Never short a green to red in a leader above the 200-day: in his Go Signal that move is the shakeout before the long.

best_conditions: A Green market reading (B18, F65). The best Go Signals come when the index itself is pulling back to its 20-day line and gets bought: his 22 Jun 2025 plan makes the index gap down bought the signal to execute on the focus list. After a correction, start with a few (F68). In Orange, A+ only; in Red, mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.

The scanner reads the daily footprint only (it needs the close), demands an open below the prior close (his newest wording describes an open above it; his good MSFT 2022-11-22 and okay AAPL 2022-08-24 are its negative fixtures), has no 200-day gate (its positive MSFT 2022-11-17 was under it), fires without the turn (daily_proxy), uses a $2 floor, a stop exactly on the low and 2R/3R targets. Its 92% precision is recognition of daily footprints by AI judges, not results. D-004.
